name: AotArtifactWriteFailed
title: AOT Artifact Error
messageFormat: Failed to write AOT artifact to '{0}': {1}

name: ObjectCreationNotSupported
title: Object creation not supported in GPU kernels
messageFormat: Object creation ('new') is not supported in GPU kernels. Only struct instantiation and SharedMemory<T> are allowed.

name: StringNotSupported
title: String usage not supported in GPU kernels
messageFormat: The string type is not supported in GPU kernels

name: UnsupportedSyntax
title: Unsupported syntax in GPU kernel
messageFormat: The syntax '{0}' is not supported in GSharp GPU kernels

name: KernelReturnMustBeVoidOrBlittable
title: GpuKernel return type must be void or blittable
messageFormat: Method '{0}' is marked with [GpuKernel] but returns unsupported type '{1}'. GpuKernel methods must return void or an unmanaged blittable type.

name: GpuBigIntExprDirectAssignment
title: GpuBigIntExpr must be assigned via .Value
messageFormat: Direct assignment or local declaration of GpuBigIntExpr is not supported. Use 'gpuResult.Value = expr' to evaluate the expression directly into the target buffer.

name: InlinePtxArgumentMustBeStringLiteral
title: InlinePtx argument must be a string literal
messageFormat: The argument to Gpu.InlinePtx must be a string literal or an interpolated string literal

name: ForeachNotSupported
title: Foreach is not allowed in GPU kernels
messageFormat: The GPU method '{0}' uses a foreach loop. Use a standard for loop instead to avoid IEnumerator allocation overhead.

name: LinqNotSupported
title: LINQ is not allowed in GPU kernels
messageFormat: The GPU method '{0}' uses LINQ query expressions, which are not supported on the GPU

name: ImplicitVarNeedsSuffix
title: Implicit var with literal needs suffix
messageFormat: The variable '{0}' is implicitly typed (var) and assigned a numeric literal without a suffix. Use a suffix (like 'U' or 'UL') or explicitly type it as 'uint' or 'ulong'.

name: PreludeMissing
title: GSharp Prelude missing
messageFormat: Could not find exactly one embedded resource ending with 'Prelude.cu' in {0}. Found {1}.

name: MacroLambdaRequiresParameter
title: Macro lambda requires a parameter
messageFormat: {0} lambda must declare a parameter for the loop variable

name: MacroArgumentMustBeConstant
title: Macro arguments must be compile-time constants
messageFormat: The argument '{0}' of macro '{1}' must be a compile-time constant

name: ExcessiveSharedMemoryWarning
title: Excessive static shared memory usage
messageFormat: The kernel allocates {0} bytes of static shared memory, which exceeds the recommended limit of {1} bytes. This may cause kernel launch failure or reduce occupancy.

name: LargeStructByValueWarning
title: Large struct passed by value (Deprecated)
messageFormat: The parameter '{0}' is a struct of size {1} bytes. Passing large structs by value to a GPU kernel can consume excessive constant memory. Consider passing by reference (ref) or using an array pointer. (Deprecated, replaced by GSH0064)

name: AutoAllocateReturnInLoopWarning
title: Auto-allocated array in loop
messageFormat: The method '{0}' returns an auto-allocated array and is called inside a loop. This will cause implicit heap allocations each iteration and may trigger GC spikes. Consider pre-allocating the array and passing it as an argument.

name: UnrollFactorMustBeNonNegativeConstant
title: Unroll factor must be a non-negative compile-time constant
messageFormat: The argument 'factor' of Gpu.Hint.Unroll must be a compile-time non-negative integer

name: UnrollHintMustPrecedeLoop
title: Unroll hint must precede a loop
messageFormat: Gpu.Hint.Unroll must immediately precede a for, while, or do-while loop

name: HostIntrinsicCallError
title: GPU intrinsic called from host
messageFormat: The GPU intrinsic '{0}' cannot be called from a host method

name: ManualEnumeratorNotSupported
title: Manual GetEnumerator calls are not supported
messageFormat: Explicit calls to GetEnumerator() are not supported in GPU kernels. Use a foreach loop instead so that the transpiler emits the enumerator loop for foreach itself.

name: MissingIDisposable
title: Missing IDisposable implementation
messageFormat: A class holds a disposable GPU resource (e.g., GpuWorkspace) but does not implement IDisposable

name: UndisposedField
title: Undisposed GPU resource (Deprecated)
messageFormat: The Dispose() method does not explicitly invoke .Dispose() on all owned GPU resources (Deprecated, replaced by composite scopes)

name: UndisposedGpuScope
title: Undisposed GPU scope
messageFormat: The Dispose() method must explicitly invoke .Dispose() on the owned IGpuResourceScope '{0}'

name: PropertyGetterSideEffect
title: Property getter side-effect
messageFormat: Property getters must not allocate disposable resources

name: CastOperatorSideEffect
title: Cast operator side-effect
messageFormat: Implicit or explicit cast operators must not allocate disposable resources

name: UnguardedMultiAllocation
title: Unguarded multi-allocation
messageFormat: Multiple allocations in a constructor must be guarded with try-catch to avoid partial leaks

name: StaticDisposableAllocation
title: Static disposable allocation
messageFormat: Static fields must not allocate disposable resources

name: DisposingBorrowedResource
title: Disposing borrowed resource
messageFormat: Disposing a borrowed resource creates a double-dispose hazard. If taking ownership, use [TakesOwnership].

name: DisposableInDim
title: Disposable resource in Default Interface Method
messageFormat: Default Interface Methods (DIM) cannot take ownership or dispose of resources

name: ManualUnmanagedAllocation
title: Manual unmanaged allocation detected
messageFormat: Manual unmanaged allocation detected (e.g., Gpu.Unsafe.Malloc). Ensure corresponding Free() is called to prevent VRAM leaks.

name: SyncGridRequiresCooperativeKernel
title: Gpu.SyncGrid requires [GpuKernel(Cooperative = true)]
messageFormat: The method '{0}' calls Gpu.SyncGrid but is not marked with [GpuKernel(Cooperative = true)]. Grid synchronization requires a cooperative kernel launch.

name: DirectGpuKernelInvocation
title: Direct invocation of [GpuKernel] is prohibited
messageFormat: Do not call [GpuKernel] method '{0}' directly. Use the generated 'Launch{0}' launcher method instead.

name: UnrolledLoopMustBeStatic
title: Unrolled loop bounds must be statically deterministic
messageFormat: The bounds of the loop marked with Gpu.Hint.Unroll cannot be statically determined. Loop conditions must rely on compile-time constants or [GpuConstexpr] parameters.

name: UnrolledLoopMayBeIgnored
title: Unrolled loop may be silently ignored
messageFormat: The loop marked with Gpu.Hint.Unroll contains dynamic control flow (break, return, goto) and may be silently ignored by the nvcc compiler

name: ParamsModifierNotSupported
title: The 'params' modifier is prohibited in GPU device code
messageFormat: The parameter '{0}' in method '{1}' uses the 'params' modifier, which incurs heap allocation. Use parameter structs, fixed buffers, or explicit arguments instead.

name: ParallelDependentCallFromSingleThreadContext
title: Cannot call parallel-dependent processing from a single-thread context
messageFormat: The method or operator '{0}' depends on parallel execution (e.g., GridStrideLoop or SyncGrid) and cannot be called from within a single-thread context

name: KernelClassMustBePartial
title: Kernel class must be partial
messageFormat: The class '{0}' containing [GpuKernel] methods must be declared as partial to support source generation of contexts and launch methods.

name: DivergentBarrierProhibited
title: Divergent barriers are prohibited
messageFormat: Gpu.SyncThreads(), or a call to a device function that reaches it, cannot be placed inside a conditional branch or an operand that only some threads evaluate ('&&', '||', '??', '?:'). This causes undefined behavior on the GPU and deadlocks the CPU emulator.

name: ExceptionHandlingInKernelProhibited
title: Exception handling is not supported in GPU kernels
messageFormat: The try-catch-finally construct is not supported in GPU kernels. Exceptions cannot be thrown or caught on the GPU.

name: CrossBarrierRefStructProhibited
title: ref structs cannot be held across barrier synchronization
messageFormat: A ref or ref struct variable '{0}' cannot be held across a Gpu.SyncThreads() barrier. This is restricted by the C# state machine model.

name: CrossBarrierGotoProhibited
title: goto statements cannot cross barrier synchronization
messageFormat: A goto statement cannot jump across a Gpu.SyncThreads() barrier. Ensure the goto label and statement are within the same barrier phase.

name: CrossBarrierLocalPointerProhibited
title: Stack pointers cannot be held across barrier synchronization
messageFormat: A pointer to a local variable or stackalloc block cannot cross a Gpu.SyncThreads() barrier because the CPU emulator rewinds the stack frame.

name: ExternalBarrierCallProhibited
title: Gpu.SyncThreads() cannot be called from methods that are not GPU code
messageFormat: Gpu.SyncThreads() can only be called within a [GpuKernel] or [GpuDeviceFunction] method or their local functions. Other methods are not lowered into the CPU state machine.

name: FixedBlockBarrierProhibited
title: Gpu.SyncThreads() cannot be called inside a fixed block
messageFormat: Gpu.SyncThreads() cannot be called inside a fixed block. The GC pin is released when the CPU emulator suspends, causing potential access violations upon resume.

name: RecursiveBarrierProhibited
title: Recursive local functions cannot contain Gpu.SyncThreads()
messageFormat: The local function '{0}' is recursive and contains or calls Gpu.SyncThreads(). This prevents static AST inlining for state machine generation.

name: AsyncYieldInKernelProhibited
title: async, await, and yield return are prohibited in GPU kernels
messageFormat: The async and await keywords are not supported in GPU methods, and yield is supported only in a [GpuDeviceFunction] that returns IEnumerable<T>.

name: LockStatementInKernelProhibited
title: The lock statement is prohibited in GPU kernels
messageFormat: The lock statement is not supported in GPU kernels. Use atomic operations provided by the Gpu.Atomic class instead.

name: InternalCompilerError
title: Source Generator Internal Error
messageFormat: Internal compiler error in G# Transpiler: {0}

name: InvalidTakesOwnershipTarget
title: [TakesOwnership] applied to non-IDisposable type
messageFormat: [TakesOwnership] can only be applied to types that implement IDisposable

name: TakesOwnershipOnlyAllowedOnConstructors
title: [TakesOwnership] is only allowed on constructor parameters
messageFormat: [TakesOwnership] is only supported on constructor parameters for static lifecycle management

name: TakesOwnershipByRefNotSupported
title: Cannot take ownership of a reference parameter
messageFormat: Cannot take ownership of a reference parameter (ref, in, out)

name: NativeApiYamlSyntaxError
title: Native API definition is not valid YAML
messageFormat: Native API definition '{0}' could not be parsed: {1}

name: NativeApiSchemaViolation
title: Native API definition violates the schema
messageFormat: Native API definition '{0}' is invalid: {1}

name: InlinePtxNotSupportedByDialect
title: Gpu.InlinePtx is not supported by the target dialect
messageFormat: Gpu.InlinePtx is not supported by the '{0}' dialect; the call is replaced with a runtime failure

name: DoubleUnderscoreIdentifier
title: Identifier containing '__' is reserved
messageFormat: '{0}' contains '__', which is reserved for the G# compiler and the C++ implementation; rename it

name: CppKeywordIdentifier
title: GPU method name is a C++ keyword (Deprecated)
messageFormat: '{0}' is a keyword in C++/CUDA and cannot be used as a GPU method name. (Deprecated, method names are renamed automatically)

name: MalformedTrustedKey
title: Malformed trusted key line
messageFormat: Line {1} of '{0}' is not a valid trusted key: {2}

name: DuplicateAotContextName
title: Two structs share one AotContexts name
messageFormat: The structs '{0}' and '{1}' both map to '{2}' in '{3}'. Rename one of the structs; AotContexts drops a trailing 'Context', namespaces and type arguments.

name: IndistinguishableKernelOverloads
title: Kernel overloads cannot be told apart by their launch wrappers
messageFormat: The [GpuKernel] overloads '{0}' and '{1}' produce the same {2} launch wrapper signature. Rename one of the kernels.

name: UserDefinedOperatorNotSupported
title: User-defined operators are not supported in GPU code
messageFormat: The user-defined operator '{0}' of '{1}' is not supported in GPU code. Call a [GpuDeviceFunction] method instead.

name: RecursiveDeviceFunctionBarrierProhibited
title: Device functions that reach a barrier cannot be recursive
messageFormat: The device function '{0}' reaches Gpu.SyncThreads() or a warp shuffle and calls itself directly or through other device functions. The CPU state machine needs a frame of static size for every call.

name: SuspendingCallInUnsupportedContext
title: A call that suspends at a barrier is not supported in this context
messageFormat: The device function '{0}' reaches Gpu.SyncThreads() or a warp shuffle, so it cannot be called {1}. The CPU state machine can resume such a call only in the statements of a kernel or device function body, including the operands of '&&', '||' and '?:'.

name: SharedMemoryDeclarationsShareLine
title: Shared memory declarations on one line share a buffer in managed execution
messageFormat: This SharedMemory<T> declaration is on the same line as another one of '{0}'. Under managed execution a device function without barriers identifies a declaration only by its file, line and method name, so both get the same buffer. Put each declaration on its own line.

name: KernelParameterSpaceExceeded
title: Kernel parameters exceed the parameter space limit
messageFormat: The parameters of kernel '{0}' take {1} bytes, which exceeds the {2}-byte kernel parameter limit. Pass large data through an array or a device buffer instead of by value.

name: StaticMemberAccessNotSupported
title: Non-const static fields and properties are not supported in GPU code
messageFormat: The static member '{0}.{1}' cannot be accessed in GPU code because static fields and properties reside in host memory. Use a 'const' field or pass the value as a kernel parameter.

name: InstanceDeviceFunctionNotSupported
title: Instance [GpuDeviceFunction] methods are not supported
messageFormat: The method '{0}.{1}' is marked with [GpuDeviceFunction] but is an instance method. Mark the method as 'static' and pass the struct as a parameter.

name: DiscardedDisposableAllocation
title: Disposable resource is created and discarded
messageFormat: The '{0}' created here is discarded without being bound to a variable, so it can never be disposed

name: UndisposedDisposableLocal
title: Disposable local is never disposed
messageFormat: The local '{0}' owns a disposable resource but leaves its scope without being disposed. Use 'using', call Dispose(), or transfer ownership.

name: SharedMemoryDisposableNotSupported
title: SharedMemory element type must not be disposable
messageFormat: SharedMemory<T> cannot hold the disposable type '{0}'. Shared memory is released with the thread block, so its elements are never disposed.

name: IteratorShapeNotSupported
title: Iterator method must be a static [GpuDeviceFunction] returning IEnumerable<T> with a value-type element
messageFormat: Iterator method '{0}' is not supported on the GPU: {1}.

name: IteratorValueMustBeEnumeratedInPlace
title: Iterator value must be consumed directly by foreach
messageFormat: The iterator value '{0}' cannot be passed, returned, reassigned, or selected conditionally; enumerate it directly with foreach (or bind it once to a local and foreach that local).

name: IteratorBodyConstructNotSupported
title: Unsupported construct in or around an iterator
messageFormat: Construct '{0}' is not supported inside an iterator or a foreach over an iterator.

name: IteratorExpansionTooLarge
title: Iterator expansion copies the foreach body too many times
messageFormat: Expanding the iterator '{0}' at this foreach would copy the loop body {1} times (limit {2})

name: CopyAsyncWaitGroupCountOutOfRange
title: CopyAsyncWaitGroup count must be a compile-time constant between 0 and 7
messageFormat: The argument 'pendingGroups' of Gpu.CopyAsyncWaitGroup must be a compile-time integer constant between 0 and 7

name: InvalidCopyAsyncArgument
title: Gpu.CopyAsync requires a SharedMemory<T> destination and a global memory source
messageFormat: The argument '{0}' of Gpu.CopyAsync is not valid: {1}.

name: UnsupportedWarpMatrixOperation
title: Unsupported warp matrix fragment or operation
messageFormat: '{0}' is not a supported warp matrix fragment or operation: {1}.

name: DivergentDynamicSharedMemory
title: Dynamic SharedMemory<T> reached by only some threads or with a thread-dependent count
messageFormat: {0}. On CUDA each thread places the dynamic SharedMemory<T> regions of its block in the order it first reaches them, with the count it computes, so threads that reach them differently may disagree on where a region is.

name: StructLayoutNotRepresentable
title: Struct cannot be laid out on the device
messageFormat: The struct '{0}' cannot be laid out on the device: {1}.

name: FieldTypeHasNoDeviceRepresentation
title: Struct field type has no device representation
messageFormat: The type '{0}' of field '{1}' has no device representation.

name: StructArrayConvertedPerElement
title: Struct array is converted element by element
messageFormat: The array of '{0}' is converted element by element because its host and device layouts differ ({1}). Reorder the fields or avoid array fields to transfer it as one block.

name: StructArrayFieldAllocatedPerElement
title: Struct array allocates the array field of each element
messageFormat: Each element of the array of '{0}' allocates and copies its array field '{1}' separately.

name: StructTransferNotSupportedOnCpu
title: Struct cannot be passed to a CPU kernel yet
messageFormat: The struct '{0}' cannot be passed to a kernel on the CPU dialect yet because its host and device layouts differ ({1}). The CPU launcher copies it in the host layout, so the kernel would read garbled values.

name: DeviceFunctionNotExported
title: Device code of another assembly is not exported
messageFormat: '{0}' is declared in '{1}', whose G# device code export holds no record of it. Build '{1}' with this version of G#, without GSharpExportDeviceCode=false; if it already exports device code, its build reported GSH0048 for '{0}', or '{0}' is a construction of a generic struct that '{1}' does not use itself.

name: DeviceExportUnusable
title: Device code of another assembly cannot be used
messageFormat: The device code of '{0}' in '{1}' cannot be used: {2}.

name: DeviceExportNameCollision
title: Device code of two assemblies has the same C++ name
messageFormat: '{0}' of '{1}' and the same path in '{2}' both become the C++ name '{3}'. Rename the namespace or the type in one of them.

name: WarpShuffleWidthNotPowerOfTwo
title: Warp shuffle width must be 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32
messageFormat: The width of Warp.{0} is {1}; it must be 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32. CUDA leaves the result of a shuffle with any other width undefined.

name: StackLinqChainTooDeep
title: StackLinq method chain is too deep
messageFormat: StackLinq method chain exceeds the maximum allowed depth of {0}. Too many nested operators will cause template instantiation limits and compiler crashes. Consider breaking the query into multiple variables.
description: Excessive method chaining on StackLinq types can lead to compiler resource exhaustion during C++ transpilation.
